gap: No result ChatGPT got says that the BLUETTI AC50P ($339) is out of stock on BLUETTI's US store. None of them gives the AC50P's solar-input voltage limit either, but that limit (open-circuit voltage 12–28 V, which would block most series and higher-voltage panels) could not be confirmed on a maker page I opened.
standout_why: I opened three cited pages. powerbencher.com (best 500Wh) says 'No maximum solar input appears in the specification we compared' for the Jackery Explorer 500 v2. It lists solar caps for other models (220 W, 300 W) but gives no panel voltage ranges, connector types or expansion support. powerstations.reviews lists the RIVER 2 Max at 220 W solar and not expandable, and the AC50B at 200 W with a 20 ms UPS switchover. It has no voltage range or connector, and the AC50P and Jackery 500 v2 were not in the part I could read. The HSN EcoFlow chart PDF is an image with no readable text. stationarena.com would not load (certificate error). So none of the rival pages states the voltage window or connector, the panel exclusions, or which accessory fits which model. The only compatibility facts I could actually confirm (an out-of-stock flag and a carrying-case fit) are minor. The fact that would matter, the AC50P's 28 V open-circuit voltage cap, appeared only in search snippets, because the maker pages were rate-limited (HTTP 429) or missing (HTTP 404).
decides: The stock status changes the answer now: BLUETTI's US store shows the AC50P, ChatGPT's 'higher AC output' pick, as unavailable today at $339, and its $549 SP100L solar kit is unavailable too. If BLUETTI's manual confirms the 12–28 V open-circuit voltage input, solar buyers should match the AC50P only to a single low-voltage 100–200 W panel, never panels wired in series. On the Jackery 500 v2 and RIVER 2 Max, nothing I confirmed changes the pick.
